sections.heading: 1. Purpose and Scope
sections.body: This System and Communications Protection Policy defines the requirements for protecting the integrity and confidentiality of {system_name} operated by {org_name}. This policy applies to all system components within the boundary defined as {boundary} and specifically addresses the protection of {cui_description}.

sections.heading: 2. Boundary Protection and Network Control

questions.prompt: How are communications monitored and controlled at external and internal boundaries?
How are publicly accessible components logically or physically separated from internal networks?
How is the 'deny by default' network traffic policy implemented?

sections.body: Communications at external and internal boundaries are managed via {boundary_monitoring_method}. Publicly accessible components are isolated using {public_subnet_config}. Network traffic is restricted by {default_deny_implementation}.

sections.heading: 3. Architectural Design and Functional Separation

questions.prompt: What architectural designs or engineering principles are used to promote security?
How is system management functionality separated from general user functionality?

sections.body: The system employs {security_design_principles} to ensure effective information security. Separation of management and user functions is achieved through {mgmt_separation_method}, and shared resource information transfer is prevented by system design.

sections.heading: 4. Cryptography and Transmission Security

questions.prompt: What cryptographic mechanisms protect CUI during transmission?
How are cryptographic keys established and managed?
How is FIPS-validated cryptography employed for CUI confidentiality?

sections.body: CUI in transit is protected by {crypto_transmission_standard}. Cryptographic keys are handled via {key_management_process}. Confidentiality is ensured using {fips_validation_detail} to meet FIPS requirements.

sections.heading: 5. Session Management and Remote Connectivity

questions.prompt: How is split tunneling prevented for remote devices?
What are the time-out periods or conditions for terminating network connections?

sections.body: Remote connections are restricted to prevent split tunneling via {split_tunneling_prevention}. Network sessions are terminated based on {session_termination_policy}.

sections.heading: 6. Specialized Technology Controls

questions.prompt: How is remote activation of collaborative devices prohibited and indicated?
How is the use of mobile code controlled and monitored?
How is the use of VoIP technologies controlled and monitored?

sections.body: Collaborative devices are managed via {collab_device_control}. Mobile code usage is governed by {mobile_code_monitoring}, and VoIP technologies are monitored through {voip_monitoring}.

sections.heading: 7. Protection of Data at Rest

questions.prompt: How is the confidentiality of CUI at rest protected?

sections.body: The confidentiality of CUI at rest is maintained through {rest_confidentiality_method}.
